name: priority-is-ignored
why: the key does not contain the priority: first come first served.

edits.old: key = {-static_cast<int>(priority), next_sequence_++};  // highest priority first, then first come first served

name: lowest-priority-first
why: the priority is not negated: Low runs before High.

name: last-in-first-out-within-a-priority
why: the newest job of a priority runs first.

edits.old: key = {-static_cast<int>(priority), next_sequence_++};  // highest priority first, then first come first served

name: cancel-leaves-the-future-unfinished
why: the job is removed from the queue, but its handle is never told: get() throws a broken_promise error (or waits).

name: cancel-says-true-for-a-running-job
why: cancel() reports success even when the job is already running.

edits.old: if (it == queue_.end()) return false;  // already started (or finished, or cancelled)

name: cancel-is-not-counted
why: the cancelled counter is not updated by cancel().

name: discard-leaves-the-handles-hanging
why: the queue is emptied but the handles are not told: they never get JobCancelled.

edits.old: for (auto& task : discarded) task->cancel_with_exception();  // outside the lock: this wakes threads that wait on the futures

name: drain-drops-the-queued-jobs
why: the workers leave as soon as the stop flag is set, with jobs still in the queue.

edits.old: if (queue_.empty()) return;  // stopping, and nothing left to run

name: shutdown-does-not-wake-the-workers
why: sleeping workers never see the stop flag: the join waits for ever.

edits.old: work_available_.notify_all();  // sleeping workers must see the stop flag

name: submit-after-shutdown-is-accepted
why: the job is queued although no worker will ever run it.

edits.old: if (stopping_) throw std::runtime_error("the scheduler has been shut down");

name: wait-idle-ignores-running-jobs
why: wait_idle returns as soon as the queue is empty, while jobs are still running.

name: idle-is-never-announced
why: a worker that finishes the last job does not wake the threads that sit in wait_idle.

name: failed-jobs-count-as-completed
why: a job that threw is counted among the completed ones.

name: pending-includes-the-running-jobs
why: pending() adds the running jobs to the queue length.

name: submit-without-the-lock
why: the queue is changed by several threads at once: a data race.

name: idle-workers-spin
why: a worker without work loops (unlock, yield, lock) instead of sleeping.

edits.old:
work_available_.wait(lock, [this] { return stopping_ || !queue_.empty(); });
                if (queue_.empty()) return;  // stopping, and nothing left to run

name: a-thread-for-every-job
why: each job gets a new detached thread; the workers do nothing.

name: wait-without-a-predicate
why: the worker waits for any wake-up and does not look at the queue (Clean tier, and a lost wake-up).

name: the-job-runs-under-the-lock
why: the mutex is held while the job runs: jobs cannot run at the same time, and a job that submits or cancels deadlocks.
